item.title: Micah Parsons: I want to make sure all the small things are fixed before returning
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Parsons said he'd play if the Super Bowl was this week, but wants to be sure "everything is right."
item.content:encoded:
Micah Parsons called Week 6 a realistic date for him to return from last season's torn ACL over the summer, but the Packers defensive end won't be back on the field ahead of Sunday night's game against the Cowboys.

While there was added resonance for many because Parsons used to play for Dallas, he said on this week's episode of his The Edge podcast that made "the game bigger than what it was." He said it is "just another game" to him and that his focus is solely on getting back to feeling totally healthy even if he feels like he would be ready to go if this was the final game of the season.

"The biggest thing that people worried about with me, they're like, 'Man, why ain't he back yet?’ If the Super Bowl was this week, I'm playing in the Super Bowl," Parsons said. "But it's just about me making sure I have all the small things fixed first. What a lot of people don't figure out is, it's not just the ACL. It's like, why did the ACL happen? What was weak? Because it all works together. It's a chain. And throughout the history of ACL, they notice if you come back early, there tends to be an overcompensation injury on the other side. Or it could be on the same side. . . . We just gonna make sure everything is right before — It's like, what's the point of getting me back for four weeks and then next thing you know, my groin’s bothering me. I have a core muscle, now I’m missing.”

The Packers have a road game in Detroit in Week 7 and a quick turnaround to a Thursday night home game against the Panthers in Week 8. That closes out their October games and that could point to a Parsons return for the second half of the regular season.

item.title: Marlon Humphrey: Kyle Hamilton got excited when Tua Tagovailoa entered the game
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton sealed the Week 5 win over the Falcons by intercepting quarterback Tua Tagovailoa in overtime.
item.content:encoded:
Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton sealed the Week 5 win over the Falcons by intercepting quarterback Tua Tagovailoa in overtime. Hamilton apparently knew it was coming.

Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey explained on his podcast that Hamilton perked up when Tua entered the game for starter Michael Penix Jr.

Humphrey, who took no pleasure in bashing his "'Bama brother," said Hamilton had a clear reaction when he noticed that Tagovailoa was replacing Penix, who suffered a rib injury in the fourth quarter.

"Kyle was like, 'Tua in the game.' Like he knew he was gonna get a pick. He literally was like, 'Oh, he's gonna throw me one.' Like, he was so excited. It was the most excited I've probably seen Kyle. . . . He basically knew he was gonna get a pick."

And Hamilton did, on Tua's second throw of overtime. It moved the Ravens to 4-1, putting Baltimore in sole possession of first place in the AFC North.

item.title: Troy Aikman seems to confirm he'll be leaving ESPN
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Aikman says he looks forward to "where my next landing spot will be."
item.content:encoded:
At a time when a sense is growing that Troy Aikman will be leaving ESPN/ABC after the 2026 season, Aikman seems to be dealing with a vague situation in the same way a Hall of Fame quarterback would.

By not shying away from it, and by not mincing words.

Appearing Thursday morning on 96.7 The Ticket in Dallas, Aikman was specifically asked about Wednesday's account of tension between him and 25-year on-air partner Joe Buck, which reportedly resulted in a recent argument between them.

“There’s probably a time and a place for all that," Aikman said, via Joseph Hoyt of the Dallas Morning News. "I don’t know if now is the time. I don’t know if it’s hard to figure out kind of what happened. I’ll broadcast through this season and I’ll be a free agent at the end of the year and kind of see what happens. I’m looking forward to whatever the rest of this season does hold and the Super Bowl and all that and where my next landing spot may be.”

While Aikman opted not to address the situation with Buck — while also not denying the existence of tension — Aikman's words strongly suggest that he plans to leave Monday Night Football when his contract expires after Super Bowl LXI.

He said he'll "be a free agent." He said he'll look forward to "where my next landing spot will be."

When Aikman addressed the situation last month, after news emerged that Buck had signed a new five-year deal, Aikman's approach had more of a wait-and-see vibe. Now, the message seems to be more like, "See you later."

It's stunning that all of this is coming to a head with so many weeks left in the 2026 season. Throw in the fact that ESPN is televising its first-ever Super Bowl, and the Buck-Aikman relationship becomes a focal point as the year continues to unfold.

It all culminates in a four-hour broadcast that will be watched by well over 100 million people, and that could end with Aikman singing off not by signing Turn Out The Lights, The Party’s Over but by quoting the chorus of Take This Job And Shove It.

item.title: John Harbaugh: We'd be negligent if we didn't see if J.J. McCarthy can help us
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Quarterback J.J.
item.content:encoded:
Quarterback J.J. McCarthy played a handful of snaps for the Giants in last Sunday's tie with the Commanders and it sounds like the team is going to keep making plans to sprinkle him into their offensive plans.

McCarthy didn't make much of an impact — two carries for two yards and two plays wiped out by penalties — in his five snaps, but his ability as a runner is a wrinkle that Jameis Winston does not offer and head coach John Harbaugh said it behooves the Giants to find ways to get something out of every player on the active roster.

"The benefits of it? It's a change of pace," Harbaugh said, via a transcript from the team. "What you saw is probably not all we have for him right now. Whether or not he's out there or not will be determined based on whatever happens. But we'll see if it's something that can help us. One thing about it, to me, it's like, what's the benefit of not doing everything you can to use all the guys you have? We're always going to be searching for opportunities to use our players, give them an opportunity to help us win games. I think we'd be negligent if we didn't try to do that."

McCarthy has only been with the Giants for a couple of weeks, so there's a limited menu to choose from at this point and the Commanders didn't seem thrown by anything that McCarthy did while he was in the game. As that expands, McCarthy's chances of making a difference offensively should grow as well.

item.title: Jalen Hurts won't say much about "very unique" calf injury that was disclosed last Friday
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Last week's injury report for the Eagles included a curious designation on Friday.
item.content:encoded:
Last week's injury report for the Eagles included a curious designation on Friday. And Wednesday's comments from the player at the center of the issue served only to make it more curious.

Quarterback Jalen Hurts was listed as fully participating in Friday's practice before the game against the Jaguars with a calf injury. He had no injury designation for Sunday's game in London, and he was never downgraded to questionable or doubtful.

When the question came up during his midweek press conference, here's what Hurts said: "It was a very unique experience, to say the least. I don't want to get into the details of kind of leading up to the game and whatnot, but got nicked up in the Rams game."

There's a lot there, in not that many words. What would be "very unique" about a calf injury that didn't impact his practice reps? And why would it be a big secret?

The complicating factor is that the Eagles flew to London on Friday. Did he require medical care in London? Would it be something that the team doctors were able to provide? Did he have to visit a local hospital for it?

He said he was "nicked up" during the Rams game, but he wasn't on the injury report for Wednesday or Thursday. Was is it that could have happened on Sunday that would have resulted in symptoms on Friday. (A condition like compartment syndrome typically surfaces much more quickly.)

Regardless, plenty of questions flow from what seems to be very innocuous and basic on the surface. Hurts's words deepen the mystery.

He remains on the Week 6 injury report, in advance of Sunday's game against the Panthers. Hurts was listed as a full participant in Wednesday's practice, due to the calf injury.

Whatever the explanation is, there's clearly more to the story than what the team has disclosed. And the NFL doesn't require much more than the bare-bones contents of the injury report.

item.title: Shedeur Sanders hires an agent
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders has hired an agent, ESPN's Adam Schefter reports.
item.content:encoded:
Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders has hired an agent, ESPN's Adam Schefter reports.

Sanders has signed with Adie von Gontard, CEO of Young Money APAA Sports, to represent him. Sanders previously did not have an agent, going through the NFL Draft and the first part of his career self-represented.

Sanders' former Colorado teammate, Jacksonville's Travis Hunter, also signed with the same agency.

This change for Sanders calls to mind now-Texans receiver Marvin Harrison Jr., who also had been self-represented until recently. Harrison hiring an agent helped facilitate a trade from Arizona to Houston.

While the Browns have not shown an interest in moving Sanders — with recent reports noting the team would like to keep and continue developing him — Sanders hiring an agent now could streamline the process for any potential transaction down the line.

item.title: Nick Caserio: Marvin Harrison Jr. trade was finalized on Friday
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Deal was done before initial half-reports that failed to name destination.
item.content:encoded:
Yes, the trade that sent receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. from the Cardinals to the Texans was fully in place before Sunday. As it turns out, it was fully in place before Saturday.

Via Cole Thompson of USA Today, Texans G.M. Nick Caserio said in an appearance on 95.7 The Fan in Houston that the trade was finalized on Friday evening. Caserio said that the Cardinals wanted to wait until Sunday to announce it.

Most importantly, Caserio pushed back against the theory that the deal hinged on the Texans beating the Titans on Sunday.

"What happened in the game had zero bearing on the outcome," Caserio said. "Like, we're not going to agree to something and then see what happens in a game and then back out of it."

Caserio's comments make the initial half-report from ESPNFL even more bizarre. It's possible, if not likely, that the folks who broke the news that the Cardinals would be trading Harrison but who didn't identify the destination knew damn well where Harrison was going, but agreed not to name the Texans as part of the dealmaking that often happens when, coincidentally, the #insiders trade discretion for future considerations.

It didn't take much effort (which qualified me for the assignment) to get to the bottom of the question of where Harrison was being traded.

Bottom line? Per Caserio, the deal was done on Friday night. By Saturday morning, only part of the story was reported as part of the first news that Harrison's time in Arizona had ended. It made no sense then, and it makes even less sense now.

item.title: Caleb Williams will be listed as a full practice participant Wednesday
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Bears head coach Ben Johnson hasn't named a starting quarterback for Week 6 yet, but it continues to look like it could be Caleb Williams making his return against the Falcons.
item.content:encoded:
Bears head coach Ben Johnson hasn't named a starting quarterback for Week 6 yet, but it continues to look like it could be Caleb Williams making his return against the Falcons.

Williams has missed the last three games with a hamstring injury, but he returned to practice as a limited participant last Friday. The Bears will only hold a walkthrough on Wednesday and Johnson told reporters at a press conference that Williams will be listed as a full participant on their estimated practice report.

Johnson said things are "still fluid" when it comes to who will start against the Falcons, but Williams remaining full once the team moves to a normal practice later this week would seem to be a good sign for his chances of playing this weekend.

Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum have handled the quarterback work in Williams's absence.

item.title: C.J. Stroud on Marvin Harrison Jr.: I don't agree with some things that are being said about him
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: When the Texans acquired Marvin Harrison Jr. from the Cardinals, they reunited the young receiver with his college quarterback, C.J.
item.content:encoded:
When the Texans acquired Marvin Harrison Jr. from the Cardinals, they reunited the young receiver with his college quarterback, C.J. Stroud.

With Harrison already set to make his debut with his new team when the Texans play the Jaguars on Sunday, the built-in chemistry he has with Stroud will likely be key for some early success.

Stroud told reporters in his Wednesday press conference that he’s happy to have Harrison.

“Everybody's been saying how much of a good dude he is, how nice he's been,” Stroud said, via transcript from the team. “It's nice to have my guy back, and I'm excited to be rolling with him.”

Stroud added that he’s “always known [Harrison] was special.”

“[W]hen he came in, he was super ahead of his game, just really mature,” Stroud said. “Him and Emeka [Egbuka] were some of the most mature freshmen that I've been around, and then just his work ethic, and it's the same thing now.”

Stroud touted Harrison’s route running as one of his top qualities.

“He gets open on time, I think he's a very quarterback friendly receiver,” Stroud said. “The better you are with getting the ball at your hands on time, the better he is. I think that's why him and I had so much success because I'm a pocket quarterback that likes to throw it to him on time. That's when he's at his best. That's one of the great things he does.”

While there is one public perception about Harrison based on his results with the Cardinals, Stroud said that he believes Harrison will be just fine with Houston.

“I don't think anybody ever is a finished product,” Stroud said. “You're always learning ways to get better. You're always learning ways to get better at what you're already good at. I think there are two different types of perspectives you can look from. You can look from the world's perspective of who people think you are or yourself. I think that's where I've learned that it doesn't really matter what people say. They can't really stop or start what you have going on. Then you have your perspective of who you think you are, who you believe you can be. I think that's more important.

“For Marvin, he knows that. He's a heck of a player. I don't agree with some of the things that are being said about him. At the end of the day, that's what people who are on the outside are saying. I'm a firm believer of really focus on what you can control and then whatever other people say or have their opinions, kudos to them. They have platforms and things that they can say on, but that doesn't really affect you unless you make it. I think he'll be fine. I try to just be [a resource] to him if I need to. He's a confident dude. He'll be fine."

item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Broncos may have cornerback Riley Moss in the lineup against the Seahawks on Thursday night, but they'll be short a couple of defensive backs even if he does play.
item.content:encoded:
The Broncos may have cornerback Riley Moss in the lineup against the Seahawks on Thursday night, but they'll be short a couple of defensive backs even if he does play.

Moss is listed as questionable due to injured ribs. Moss did not play in Week 5 and was listed as a limited practice participant all three days this week.

Cornerback Pat Surtain II (ankle) and safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) will not be in the lineup. Surtain was injured in Week 4 and has not participated in a practice since his injury. Hufanga was injured in last Sunday's win over the Chargers and a report on Wednesday indicated he is expected to miss multiple weeks.

Safety Brandon Jones (foot), defensive lineman Sai'vion Jones (shoulder), and guard Ben Powers (biceps) were all full participants in Wednesday's practice and none of them have injury designations for Thursday.

item.title: Seahawks won't activate Zach Charbonnet for Thursday night's game
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Seahawks will remain without running back Zach Charbonnet for Thursday night's game against the Broncos.
item.content:encoded:
The Seahawks will remain without running back Zach Charbonnet for Thursday night's game against the Broncos.

Charbonnet has been practicing with the team since being designated for return from the physically unable to perform list on October 1, but the team ruled him out on Wednesday. Charbonnet will need to be activated next week if he is going to return from his torn ACL this year.

The Seahawks have also ruled out linebackers Drake Thomas (ankle) and Chazz Surratt (calf). Both players were listed as out of practice all this week.

No other players on the active roster have injury designations, which leaves wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) and defensive tackle Leonard Williams (ankle) on track to play.

In addition to the injuries, the Seahawks also announced a couple of roster moves. They signed running back Velus Jones to the active roster and released wide receiver Irv Charles a day after signing Charles and releasing Jones. Charles has rejoined the practice squad and could be elevated to play on Thursday.

item.title: Seahawks tailoring playbook so Sam Darnold can make "swift decisions," avoid turnovers
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: There are a lot of things that go into winning and losing football games, but a quick glance at the Seahawks' performance in the first five weeks of the season leads to one obvious conclusion about their results.
item.content:encoded:
There are a lot of things that go into winning and losing football games, but a quick glance at the Seahawks' performance in the first five weeks of the season leads to one obvious conclusion about their results.

In their three wins, the Seahawks have turned the ball over twice but they have turned it over seven times in their two losses. Four of those turnovers in the losses have been interceptions thrown by quarterback Sam Darnold — he has five overall — and cutting down on those giveaways is at the top of the to-do list in Seattle heading into Thursday's game against the Broncos.

On Tuesday, offensive coordinator Brian Fleury said that he and Darnold are working to tailor their game plan so that it emphasizes plays that allow Darnold to feel comfortable and decisive on the field.

"It's relying more heavily on plays that we have a lot of experience with both through training camp and through the first couple weeks that he's comfortable making swift decisions and progressing through," Fleury said, via the team's website. "We're going to lean more in that direction."

The Seahawks have had chances to win both games they lost in spite of the turnovers and those chances would be a lot better if they didn't give the ball away, so turning the focus to cutting them out is a prudent response with the race for playoff positioning in the NFC already well underway.

item.title: Aaron Rodgers on injuries at wide receiver: I have a lot of trust in our options
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Steelers are heading into Week 6 short on healthy wide receivers.
item.content:encoded:
The Steelers are heading into Week 6 short on healthy wide receivers.

Michael Pittman is on injured reserve and the team is set to be without Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek as well when they take the field in Tampa this Sunday. That leaves three wideouts on the active roster, although rookie Kaden Wetjen has yet to play an offensive snap yet this season.

The team has three more wideouts on the practice squad and quarterback Aaron Rodgers expressed his faith in Brandon Smith, Brandon Johnson, and Isaiah Hodgins while discussing the team's options on Wednesday.

"I have a lot of trust in those guys," Rodgers said, via the team's website. "I've always been a fan of Brandon Johnson; he had his locker right next to mine last year and we had some great conversations. He's played and played well when he's gotten opportunities. Obviously, I know B. Smith from New York and I'm a big believer in him. And then Isaiah was here with us last year, then went to New York and made a bunch of plays. I like those guys a lot."

The Steelers' ability to weather the injuries should be helped by how Rodgers uses all of the available targets. Running back Jaylen Warren and tight end Pat Freiermuth are tied with DK Metcalf for the team lead in catches while tight end Darnell Washington has also been used frequently in the passing game.

item.title: Jeremiyah Love's lingering ankle issue could keep him out Sunday
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love did not practice on Wednesday due to a lingering ankle issue.
item.content:encoded:
Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love did not practice on Wednesday due to a lingering ankle issue.

His availability for Sunday's game against the Rams is in question.

Love's right ankle sprain from the preseason has healed, coach Mike LaFleur said, but the left ankle has bothered him the past two weeks.

"We want to get this ankle right," LaFleur said, via Darren Urban of the team website.

That could mean Love taking a week off.

He played 36 of 73 snaps in the loss to the Lions on Sunday, with 12 rushes for only 22 yards.

"I'm going to try to be as candid as possible knowing that everyone is listening to this too," LaFleur said. "He's a tough dude. But you see how he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. Imagine being a running back in the NFL and putting your foot down and cutting the way that you are capable of.

"We all agree that as much as he wants to battle, hey, let's give it a little bit of rest and see how it is as the week goes on."

Safeties Dewey Wingard (knee) and Wydett Williams Jr. (concussion) also did not practice.

Safety Kitan Crawford (ankle) and wide receiver/returner Devin Duvernay (ribs) were limited. Crawford is in his 21-day return-to-practice window.

Safety Budda Baker, outside linebacker Josh Sweat and left guard Isaac Seumalo had their usual rest day.

item.title: Tyler Shough: We can't let Gayle Benson's comments affect our daily process
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Saints owner Gayle Benson's decision to publicly air her frustrations about the team's 1-4 start earlier this week drew a lot of attention because of how blunt she was about her disappointment and how rarely she shares her views about the state of the franchise.
item.content:encoded:
Saints owner Gayle Benson's decision to publicly air her frustrations about the team's 1-4 start earlier this week drew a lot of attention because of how blunt she was about her disappointment and how rarely she shares her views about the state of the franchise.

Quarterback Tyler Shough was among those who caught what Benson had to say and he said on Wednesday that Benson "wasn't saying anything that wasn't already known" about how things have unfolded so far this season. Shough said that the team shares Benson's desire for better results and that they are not going to change their approach to the job because she has gone public with them.

"You obviously see it, it’s all over social media," Shough said. "It doesn’t affect our day-to-day process and we can't let it regardless. We win a game and you're the greatest people ever, and you lose some games and it's the worst thing ever. So I've said it before: We're going to have a really good chance to go on a run here. I think it starts with controlling what we can and all of a sudden the narrative changes, or not and we continue to slip and we've got to find a way to control that."

A trip to New Jersey to face the Giants will be the Saints' first chance to shift the narrative with a trip to Paris to face the Steelers and a bye week on tap from there. If they can get to that bye at 3-4, things should feel a little less pressured in New Orleans but the alternative won't have anyone resting easy about what kind of changes could be in the franchise's future.

item.title: Malik Willis doesn't think he has a tell despite Jordan Battle intercepting him twice
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Bengals safety Jordan Battle said before Sunday's game that he was going to time Willis's passes because of how willis pats the ball before throwing. Then Battle had two interceptions.
item.content:encoded:
Bengals safety Jordan Battle said before Sunday's game that he had identified a tendency of Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis to pat the ball before throwing, and that he was going to use that tendency to time his breaks on Willis's passes. At the time, it seemed like a foolish thing to say out loud, but Battle backed up his talk and intercepted Willis twice as the Bengals won.

Still, Willis doesn't believe he has a tell.

Asked after the game about Battle's comments, Willis indicated that he wasn't even sure who Battle was, asking a reporter to clarify which Bengals player had said he had a tell.

"Who said that?" Willis asked.

A reporter answered, "Jordan Battle."

Willis then asked, "What number?"

A reporter told Willis that Battle wears No. 27, and Willis said he didn't even realize that Battle had caught both of his interceptions. Willis incorrectly thought No. 44, linebacker Demetrius Knight, had caught one of the interceptions.

"I thought 44 caught one. I thought 44 caught a pick. Either way, you said he caught both? Let's come on," Willis said.

Willis disputed that the interceptions had anything to do with a tell. On one of the picks, Willis's hand was hit as he was throwing the ball, and on the other one, Willis felt pressure to his left, scrambled to his right and threw directly to Battle.

"That's not a tell, he caught tipped balls. Good for him, that's what defenses are supposed to do at this level," Willis said. "They battled a ball down and the second one was a scramble drill mishap. That has nothing to do with tells. I don't think I patted either one of those. I don't think those are correlated."

Willis said he had been told what Battle said but didn't put any stock in it.

"I didn't think much of it. Everybody pats the ball. That's funny. Really funny," Willis said.

It was the Bengals who had something to laugh about after the game, as Battle backed up his talk.

item.title: Texans are 1-4, but Will Anderson is playing like a Defensive Player of the Year
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Anderson leads the NFL in sacks and tackles for loss and leads the betting odds for the Defensive Player of the Year Award.
item.content:encoded:
On a Texans team that hasn't had much to celebrate this season, defensive end Will Anderson is the NFL's leading candidate for the Defensive Player of the Year award.

Anderson leads the NFL with 7.5 sacks through five games, which puts him on a record pace of 25.5 sacks in a 17-game season. Anderson has had at least half a sack in every game this season, and he's coming off his best game of the season, with three sacks on Titans quarterback Cam Ward.

Anderson, who also has 10 tackles for loss, is the first NFL player to have at least 7.5 sacks and 10 tackles for loss in his team's first five games since 2012, when J.J. Watt did it, also for the Texans.

Unlike the league MVP award, which almost always goes to the quarterback on one of the best teams in the league, the voters are willing to give the Defensive Player of the Year award to players on bad teams. Last year it was Myles Garrett on the 5-12 Browns, and this year it may go to Anderson even if the Texans don't turn things around.

The current betting odds have Anderson as the overwhelming favorite to win Defensive Player of the Year, with +125 odds. He's followed by Pittsburgh's T.J. Watt and Minnesota's Dallas Turner, both at +850.

Houston made a huge investment in Anderson, first trading two first-round picks, a second-round pick and a third-round pick to move up and draft him third overall in 2023, then signing him to a three-year, $150 million contract extension this year. On a team that has been a massive disappointment, Anderson has been a bright spot.

item.title: Jaguars are first team since the merger not to allow a 40-yard rusher in first five games
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Opposing running backs have 83 carries for 210 yards against the Jaguars this season, an average of just 2.5 yards per carry.
item.content:encoded:
No one can run the ball on the Jaguars.

Through five games this season, the most rushing yards any player has gained in a game against the Jaguars was 39, by Broncos running back Jonah Coleman.. That makes the Jaguars the first team since the 1970 AFL-NFL merger not to allow an opposing player to rush for 40 or more yards in the first five games of a season.

The last team not to allow a 40-yard rusher in the first five games was the 1969 Cowboys.

Last year, the most rushing yards any player gained in a game against the Jaguars was 74, by Colts running back Jonathan Taylor. The Jaguars have now gone 23 consecutive games, counting last year's playoff game, without allowing a 75-yard rusher.

Opposing running backs have totaled 83 carries for 210 yards against the Jaguars this season, an average of just 2.5 yards per carry. That's by far the best defense against running backs in the NFL this season.

On Sunday in London the Jaguars face the Texans, who rank 31st in the league with 395 rushing yards this season.

item.title: Al Michaels won't complain if Prime Video wants to move on
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The legendary Al Michaels continues to call the biggest of NFL games, four decades after making his debut on Monday Night Football.
item.content:encoded:
The legendary Al Michaels continues to call the biggest of NFL games, four decades after making his debut on Monday Night Football. Now in his fifth year with Thursday Night Football on Prime Video, the 81-year-old broadcasting icon realizes that, at some point, it will end.

Appearing on Wednesday's edition of The Dan Patrick Show, Michaels addressed the question of when he'll know the time has come.

“Well, either the people that I work for will tell me, or I’ll know myself, a combination,” Michaels said, via Sam Neumann of Awful Announcing. “Let’s put it this way. The folks at Amazon and Prime have been fantastic. Fantastic to me.”

After his initial three-year deal, Prime Video has extended the arrangement on a one-year basis, twice. If they don't do it again, Michaels will be fine with that.

“If they come to me and say, 'You know, it’s time for us to move on.' . . . 'You guys have been fantastic. You’ve been great.' I’ve done the NFL for 41 years, which is half my life. Love it. But you know what? At a certain time, it’s time. And if they feel it’s time, great. And if I feel it’s time, I’ll know it. And I’ll say, ‘You know what? Thanks for the memories.'"

We're the ones who should be thanking him. As we've said before, many won't appreciate how much of our sports-watching lives he has influenced until he's no longer part of it. And while there are plenty of highly competent voices out there, Michaels is one of the very best to ever do it — possibly the best of all of the play-by-play announcers.

He has been able to land in a high-profile spot after his tenure at NBC ended before he likely wanted it to. We've been able to listen to him call games for another four-plus years, thanks to the fact that Prime Video hired him.

So either he'll walk away or he'll get a nudge. Either way, Michaels's long and distinguished journey has much greater meaning than however the road ends. For me and many others, it won't be the same to go through a football season without hearing him calling a game every week.

item.title: Bradley Chubb explains his side of altercation with Alaric Jackson
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Rams offensive tackle Alaric Jackson had his suspension reduced to one game on appeal Wednesday.
item.content:encoded:
Rams offensive tackle Alaric Jackson had his suspension reduced to one game on appeal Wednesday. He will be on unpaid leave Sunday when the Rams play the Cardinals.

Bills pass rusher Bradley Chubb, who took a punch from Jackson after the game Monday night, said he learned a valuable lesson from the incident.

"Me personally, I learned I'm either going to have my hands up or wear a helmet," Chubb said, via Nick Suss of ESPN.

Chubb admitted he initiated the conversation between the two men after the Bills' 37-34 overtime victory.

"I'll tell you exactly what I said," Chubb said at the practice facility on UC Irvine's campus, where the Bills are practicing this week. "I've heard I was talking about his mom. That's not true at all. I said, 'We're gonna see y'all's ass again, and when we see you again, all that chipping ain't gonna save you. That tight end and guard is not going to save you.' He said, 'What'd you say?' I said, 'That chip's not gonna save you. The guard's not gonna save you.' And then boom."

Chubb, who hasn't heard from Jackson since the punch, said he was proud he didn't retaliate and draw a suspension of his own.

If the teams play again this season, it will be in the Super Bowl back at SoFi Stadium in February.

item.title: Four men arrested in shooting of 49ers DL Keion White in February
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Police have arrested four men in connection with the shooting of 49ers defensive lineman Keion White earlier this year, the Associated Press reports.
item.content:encoded:
Police have arrested four men in connection with the shooting of 49ers defensive lineman Keion White earlier this year, the Associated Press reports.

White was hosting a private Super Bowl party in a nightclub in San Francisco when the shooting occurred in the early morning hours of Feb. 9. White was treated at a local hospital for gunshot wounds to his ankle.

Investigators used video footage and witness statements to identify the multiple suspects with firearms who confronted White.

San Francisco Police Chief Derrick Lew said authorities arrested the suspects over the past week with the help of law enforcement agencies in Atlanta; Stockton, California; Irvine, California and Los Angeles.

Curtis Green, 35, was arrested in Irvine on Oct. 7, and two days later, authorities arrested 36-year-old Gregory Walker of Mountain House, California. Walker will be charged with assault with a semiautomatic firearm -- which prosecutors say he fired -- as well as other charges for having a gun as a felon.

Green faces misdemeanor charges of brandishing a firearm and carrying a concealed and loaded gun in public.

Two other men arrested in other jurisdictions are not yet in local custody.

White has appeared in all five games for the 49ers this season and has three sacks.

item.title: Hearing officer Derrick Brooks reduces Alaric Jackson's suspension to one game
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Jackson will miss Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
item.content:encoded:
Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson will be suspended for sucker punching Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb. But Jackson won't miss two games.

Hearing officer Derrick Brooks has reduced Jackson's suspension to one game on appeal.

It's possible that Jackson's case included evidence regarding the provocation from Chubb that preceded the approach. Chubb may have said something that made the punch less unreasonable. Or not so unreasonable to support a two-game suspension.

Jackson will still serve a one-game suspension, missing Sunday's game against the Cardinals. At a base salary of $16.822 million, he'll lose $934,555.

That may have been a factor in the final decision. Apart from the time missed, Jackson was looking at losing nearly $2 million on a two-game suspension.

Regardless, Jackson is fortunate to be missing only one game. He punched Chubb minutes after the game ended. Hot blood should have cooled by then. And Jackson likely would have been arrested if he'd done it in the parking lot instead of in the middle of the field.

item.title: 8.1 million watched Eagles-Jaguars
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Same city.
item.content:encoded:
Same city. Same stadium. Same day of the week. Same kickoff time.

Different teams. Far different numbers.

The Colts-Commanders game at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London averaged fewer than five million viewers in Week 4. In Week 5, Eagles-Jaguars generated 8.1 million viewers.

It was the second most-watched international game on NFL Network, with a 36-percent increase over the 2025 average of 6.2 million.

The series continues this weekend, when the Texans face the Jaguars at Wembley Stadium in London. In Week 7, the Steelers face the Saints in Paris.

Sunday's game lasted three hours and 42 minutes, trickling into the 1:00 p.m. ET window — and likely taking a major chunk out of the ratings for the pregame shows on ESPN, Fox, and CBS. If/when (when) the NFL secures the ability to stage 16 international games per season, the 9:30 a.m. ET window will become commonplace. At some point, it will be fair to ask whether the morning/afternoon pregame shows should go the way of the dodo bird.

With so much more analysis and content available in advance of the Sunday games than ever before, the Sunday morning/afternoon pregame shows really don't add much. They add even less when, you know, a game is being televised at the time the pregame shows are on.

Indeed, if/when (when) the NFL sells the Sunday morning European package to the highest bidder, whoever wins the rights may request that the NFL direct its other broadcast partners to stand down from 9:30 a.m. ET to 1:00 p.m. ET on every Sunday when a game is being played.
